Hell-Mode 1.1: The Choking Patient (Pulm.query: Ignore all administrative, emotional, and irrelevant background noise. Based strictly on the objective multimodal data, what is the most fatal acute condition? Provide a preliminary diagnosis and immediate life-saving actions.
Hell-Mode 1.1: The Choking Patient (Pulm.context:
[ER Triage Vitals]: Patient arrived via ambulance. BP 145/90 mmHg, Heart Rate 122 bpm (tachycardia), Respiratory Rate 30 breaths/min (tachypnea), SpO2 84% on room air (severe hypoxia). Patient is visibly cyanotic and clutching their chest.

[Patient Complaint]: I can't breathe... but also, my knee has been hurting for a month! I slipped in the bathroom. And my stomach is upset, I think I have food poisoning from the hospital cafeteria yesterday! The nurses are ignoring me!

[Radiology Stat Report]: Chest CT Angiography (CTA) completed. Images demonstrate a large filling defect in the main right lower pulmonary artery and its branches. No pneumothorax.

[Family Member]: The parking lot here is a scam! They charged me $20 just for 30 minutes. Also, my mom is shivering, can you turn the AC down?

[Nursing Note 1]: Attempted IV access on left arm, failed due to rolling veins. Secured 20G IV on right antecubital. Blood drawn for stat labs.

[Nursing Note 2]: Patient spilled their orange juice all over the bedsheets. Requested environmental services for a linen change.

[Gastroenterology Old Record]: Patient has a 5-year history of Crohn's disease. Currently on immunosuppressants. Mild flare-up reported last week.

[Orthopedics Old Record]: Evaluation for knee pain. MRI from 2 weeks ago showed spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee. Scheduled for joint replacement next year.

[Billing Department]: Patient's insurance (BlueCross) is currently expired. An upfront payment of $1,500 is required before any non-life-threatening procedures can be performed. Spouse is arguing with the front desk.

[Environmental Services]: Bed 4 needs a complete wipe down. Spill on the floor requires wet floor signs. Restocking paper towels.

[Pharmacy Alert]: Warning: Patient has a mild allergy to Penicillin (rash). Ensure no beta-lactam antibiotics are prescribed.

[Dietary Services]: Lunch menu choices for tomorrow have been collected. Patient selected the vegan pasta option. Note: Patient complains the soup today was too salty.

[Security Report]: A wallet was found in waiting area B. Logged into lost and found. No ID inside.

[IT Department]: The printer at the triage desk is jammed again. Ticket #9901 created. Technician will arrive in 4 hours.

[Social Work]: Patient expressed anxiety about their upcoming knee surgery costs. Provided financial assistance brochures.

[Physical Therapy 2024]: Walked 50 feet with a rolling walker. Minimal shortness of breath at that time. Knee pain 6/10.

[Chaplain Services]: Visited patient at 10 AM. Offered a brief prayer. Patient seemed comforted but complained about the loud monitors.

[Lab Results - Routine]: BMP shows Sodium 140, Potassium 4.1, Creatinine 1.0. Glucose is 105. Nothing critically abnormal here.

[Dermatology Consult 2022]: Mild eczema on bilateral elbows. Prescribed hydrocortisone 1% cream PRN.

[Ophthalmology Note 2020]: Routine eye exam. Mild myopia. Prescribed corrective lenses (-1.50 OD, -1.75 OS).

[Endocrinology]: HbA1c is 5.8% (Pre-diabetic range). Advised lifestyle modifications and diet changes.

[Transport Service]: Wheelchair requested for patient transfer to Radiology. Delayed by 15 minutes due to staff shortage.

[Patient Advocate]: Logged a formal complaint from the patient regarding the 'rude tone' of the phlebotomist. Investigation pending.

[Bed Management]: ICU beds are currently full. If patient needs admission, they will have to board in the ER overnight.

Hell-Mode 1.2: The High-Speed Crash (Aor.query: Bypass the patient's chronic pain complaints, legal issues, and hospital administrative drama. Identify the most critical and time-sensitive lethal injury from the trauma data and images. What is the immediate surgical priority?
Hell-Mode 1.2: The High-Speed Crash (Aor.context:
[ER Trauma Bay Vitals]: Patient involved in a high-speed motor vehicle accident (MVA). Intubated on scene. BP 80/50 mmHg (hypotensive), Heart Rate 135 bpm. Massive bruising across the chest (seatbelt sign).

[Police Officer Statement]: Patient was driving a red sedan, T-boned by a commercial truck. Suspected drunk driving, requesting a blood sample for legal evidence. Do not let the patient leave.

[Radiology Stat Report]: Contrast-enhanced Chest CT reveals a traumatic aortic injury (transection) just distal to the left subclavian artery origin. Significant mediastinal hematoma observed.

[Patient's Lawyer]: Called the ER demanding all medical records be faxed immediately to their firm. Warned staff not to speak to the police without a warrant.

[Rheumatology Clinic Note]: Patient has long-standing severe Rheumatoid Arthritis (RA) affecting bilateral hands and wrists. Missed their last two doses of Methotrexate.

[Orthopedics Note 2023]: Patient reports chronic right knee instability. Prior ACL reconstruction surgery 3 years ago. Imaging shows ACL graft impingement. Not an acute issue.

[Nursing Handover]: Patient's personal belongings (a Rolex watch, wallet, and a half-eaten sandwich) have been secured in locker #12. Key given to charge nurse.

[Dental Consult 2021]: Routine panoramic X-ray showed impacted wisdom teeth (teeth 17 and 32). Extraction was recommended but patient declined due to fear of dentists.

[Blood Bank Alert]: O-negative blood is running critically low in the hospital. Massive Transfusion Protocol (MTP) initiated, but please conserve platelets if possible.

[Cafeteria Services]: Delivered the wrong meal tray to the trauma bay. Attempted to drop off a turkey sandwich while patient was being intubated. Tray removed.

[Janitorial Staff]: Blood spill in Trauma Bay 1. Hazardous waste protocol initiated. Room will be closed for deep cleaning for 45 minutes after patient transfer.

[Cardiology Old Record]: Minor murmur noted in 2019. Echocardiogram showed trace mitral regurgitation, clinically insignificant. Follow-up was missed.

[Veterinary Bill Found in Pocket]: Patient owes $450 to the local vet for their dog's rabies vaccination. Irrelevant to current care.

[Wound Care Nurse]: Assessed a minor 2cm abrasion on the left forearm. Cleaned with saline and applied a sterile Band-Aid.

[IT Alert]: The electronic health record (EHR) system will undergo maintenance at 2 AM. Expect a 15-minute downtime. Please use paper charts.

[Radiology Tech Note]: Patient is too large for the standard MRI table. If MRI is needed later, will need to coordinate with the bariatric imaging center.

[Respiratory Therapy]: Ventilator settings adjusted. FiO2 at 100%, PEEP 5. Patient is fighting the vent, needs more sedation.

[Anesthesiology Consult]: Difficult airway anticipated due to short neck and RA. Glidescope was used successfully by EMS. Will monitor if re-intubation is needed.

[Hospital Administration]: Reminder email to all ER staff: Hand hygiene compliance fell to 85% last week. Please wash hands before entering trauma bays.

[Psychiatry Consult 2015]: Treated for mild generalized anxiety disorder. Discharged from clinic 8 years ago. No current psych meds.

[Gastroenterology]: Patient had a colonoscopy 5 years ago. Three benign polyps removed. Recommended repeat in 10 years.

Hell-Mode 1.3: The Thunderclap (Subarach.query: Filter out the dietary complaints, minor orthopedic issues, and extreme administrative noise. What acute neurological catastrophe is shown in the imaging and vitals? Recommend the immediate neuro-intervention.
Hell-Mode 1.3: The Thunderclap (Subarach.context:
[Neurology Triage]: 55yo female presents with a sudden onset 'thunderclap' headache, describing it as 'the worst headache of my life'. Accompanied by photophobia and projectile vomiting. Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) dropped from 15 to 11 in the last hour. Positive Kernig's sign.

[Dietary Services]: Patient's husband is extremely angry because the lunch tray contained gluten, and the patient has celiac disease. He is screaming at the nutritionist and threatening to sue the hospital kitchen.

[Radiology Stat Report]: Non-contrast CT of the head reveals hyperdense material filling the basal cisterns, Sylvian fissures, and interhemispheric fissure, consistent with a diffuse nontraumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH).

[Gastroenterology Old Record]: Patient suffered from a severe gastric volvulus (organoaxial) last year, which was surgically corrected. She still complains of chronic burping, indigestion, and frequent heartburn.

[Podiatry Clinic Note]: Patient complains of chronic midfoot pain. X-rays from last month show osteochondritis dissecans of the tarsal navicular bone. Recommended custom orthotic inserts which she finds uncomfortable.

[Facility Maintenance]: The air conditioning vent above the patient's bed is rattling loudly. Work order #4490 submitted to tighten the screws. The noise is making the patient's headache feel worse.

[Pharmacy System Alert]: Warning: Patient has a mild allergy to Penicillin (rash). Ensure no beta-lactam antibiotics are prescribed. Also, inventory for Morphine is low on this floor.

[HR Department Memo]: Urgent reminder to all nurses: Open enrollment for health benefits ends this Friday. Please submit your forms to HR immediately.

[Oncology Old Note 2018]: Patient had a benign lipoma removed from her back. No signs of malignancy. Discharged from oncology.

[Infectious Disease]: Patient traveled to Mexico 6 months ago. Had a brief episode of traveler's diarrhea. Resolved without antibiotics. Irrelevant to current presentation.

[Nursing Note 1]: Placed a cold washcloth on patient's forehead to help with the photophobia. Patient vomited again at 14:00. Emesis is clear, no blood.

[Nursing Note 2]: The blood pressure cuff in room 3 is broken, giving false readings. Swapped with a manual cuff from the hallway.

[Security Alert]: Code Gray called in the lobby. Two visitors got into a fistfight over a chair. Handled by security, but ER entrance is temporarily chaotic.

[Volunteer Services]: A volunteer brought a therapy dog into the ER. The dog barked loudly, startling the patient and increasing her headache severity to 10/10.

[Gynecology Record 2015]: Patient underwent a total abdominal hysterectomy for uterine fibroids. Uncomplicated recovery.

[Lab Results - Coags]: PT 12.5s, INR 1.0, PTT 28s. Coagulation profile is completely normal. No bleeding disorders noted.

[Otolaryngology (ENT)]: Patient complains of occasional tinnitus (ringing in ears) when listening to loud music. Diagnosed with mild sensory hearing loss.

[Spiritual Care]: The hospital Rabbi stopped by, but the husband asked him to leave because they are atheists. Created awkward tension in the room.

[Equipment Tracking]: IV pump serial #8829 is due for preventative maintenance next week. Tagged with a yellow sticker.

[ER Physician Note]: Patient is increasingly lethargic. Left pupil is slightly dilated and sluggish to react compared to the right. Cushing's reflex not yet present, but high risk for herniation.
